headline: 690,608 students fail SSC and equivalent exams
summary: Overall pass rate drops to 62.25%, with a significant decline in GPA-5 achievers for the fourth consecutive year.
details: The results for the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examinations have been published, revealing a overall pass rate of 62.25%.
A total of 690,608 students failed to clear the exams, marking a significant decline in overall performance.
GPA-5 achievers have decreased for the fourth straight year, with 116,676 students securing the top grade.
There is a stark contrast in performance across boards; the Dhaka Education Board recorded the highest pass rate, while the Madrasa Board recorded the lowest at 55.49%.
The Technical Board also saw a lower pass rate of 58.20%.
A worrying trend is the emergence of 312 institutions with a 'zero pass' rate, more than doubling the number of schools where no student passed.
Over half of the humanities students (59%) failed their exams, and the English pass rate remained below 75% in 7 out of 9 boards.
On a positive note, 669 institutions achieved a 100% pass rate, and girls outperformed boys in both the overall pass rate and GPA-5 achievements.
caption:
Nearly 7 lakh students failed their SSC exams this year. Pass rates and GPA-5 holders have both plummeted.

The results for the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examinations have been published, revealing a overall pass rate of 62.25%.

A total of 690,608 students failed to clear the exams, marking a significant decline in overall performance.

GPA-5 achievers have decreased for the fourth straight year, with 116,676 students securing the top grade.

There is a stark contrast in performance across boards; the Dhaka Education Board recorded the highest pass rate, while the Madrasa Board recorded the lowest at 55.49%.

The Technical Board also saw a lower pass rate of 58.20%.

A worrying trend is the emergence of 312 institutions with a 'zero pass' rate, more than doubling the number of schools where no student passed.

Over half of the humanities students (59%) failed their exams, and the English pass rate remained below 75% in 7 out of 9 boards.

On a positive note, 669 institutions achieved a 100% pass rate, and girls outperformed boys in both the overall pass rate and GPA-5 achievements.

headline: 16 Bangladeshis killed in Saudi factory fire
summary: A devastating blaze at a sofa factory in Riyadh has claimed the lives of at least 16 Bangladeshi nationals, many of whom were from Naogaon.
details: At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in the Musa Industrial Area of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
The fire broke out around 2:00 pm yesterday, killing 16 people on the spot, according to a notification from the Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry.
Of the deceased, 13 were residents of Naogaon, two were from Natore, and one was from Rajshahi.
The victims from Naogaon include Farid, Shuvo, Md Rubel Pramanik, Suman, Md Kaliyuddin, Md Mohon, Md Sumon, Minhaj, Hridoy, Shaheen, Abdul Jalil, Majidul, and Shagor.
The victims from Natore were identified as Shamim and Sabbir, while the victim from Rajshahi was named Shyamol.
The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh has expressed deep sorrow and is working closely with Saudi authorities to identify all victims.
Officials from the embassy's Labour Welfare Wing are present at the site to coordinate rescue and identification efforts.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare have confirmed that necessary arrangements will be made to repatriate the bodies to Bangladesh.
caption:
16 Bangladeshi nationals have lost their lives in a horrific sofa factory fire in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in the Musa Industrial Area of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

The fire broke out around 2:00 pm yesterday, killing 16 people on the spot, according to a notification from the Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry.

Of the deceased, 13 were residents of Naogaon, two were from Natore, and one was from Rajshahi.

The victims from Naogaon include Farid, Shuvo, Md Rubel Pramanik, Suman, Md Kaliyuddin, Md Mohon, Md Sumon, Minhaj, Hridoy, Shaheen, Abdul Jalil, Majidul, and Shagor.

The victims from Natore were identified as Shamim and Sabbir, while the victim from Rajshahi was named Shyamol.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh has expressed deep sorrow and is working closely with Saudi authorities to identify all victims.

Officials from the embassy's Labour Welfare Wing are present at the site to coordinate rescue and identification efforts.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare have confirmed that necessary arrangements will be made to repatriate the bodies to Bangladesh.
